name: Senate Palace (Tehran)
features: A freestanding marble-grid facade between two 25 m bronze columns shaped as linked chains, sculpted by André Bloc.
why: Ghiai and Foroughi's senate for Iran's parliament, the first government commission of a pioneer of Iranian modernism (Encyclopaedia Iranica).

photos.file: File:Senate Palace of Iran in Tehran.jpg

sources.quote: Ḡīāʾī’s first government commission was the Senate building (Majles-e Senā) in Tehran (1954-59), a joint project with Moḥsen Forūḡī
Although the Senate’s architect was Ghiaï, but André Bloc in his book, named also Mohsen foroughi as co-architect of the project.
Foroughi had just executed the sculptural columns, which were designed and drew by Heydar Ghiaï.
the Senate building (Majles-e Senā) in Tehran (1954-59)
Heydar Ghiaï designed the Senate House of Iran (The Parliament bulding of Islamic Republic of Iran from 1979 to 2005) in 1955.
H. Giai (Ḡīāʾī), “Palais du Sénat, Téhéran,” Architecture d’Aujourd’hui , no. 78, 1958, pp. 96-101.
It has an imposing, freestanding marble-grid facade, embraced by two twenty-five-meter high bronze columns sculpted by André Bloc (1896-1966) in the shape of enlarged linked chains.
The dome of The Senate House was one of the most technically challenging projects in Ghiaï’s entire career.

name: House of Victoria Ocampo
features: Rationalist house of bare white cubes on three levels and two terraces; a National Historic Monument since 2022.
why: The rationalist house built for the writer Victoria Ocampo; an ArchDaily AD Classic.

La construcción de la vivienda fue encargada al reconocido arquitecto argentino Alejandro Bustillo, aunque fue originalmente proyectada para otro terreno, por el célebre Le Corbusier.

la “casa racionalista” que hizo construir Victoria Ocampo en 1928

name: Plassen Cultural Centre
features: Granite on every outside surface; the roof and a stair make three open-air amphitheatres; a triple-height atrium leads to the concert hall.
why: 3XN's cultural centre in Molde, published by Dezeen.

sources.quote: by Danish architects 3XN
Architect: 3XN
3XN has designed a new new cultural center for the Norwegian city of Molde.
Official Opening: 14th of July, 2012
Construction: 2009 – 2012
The architects used granite for all the exterior surfaces
Together with the building's roof, an existing staircase next to the building constitute a total of three outdoor amphitheatres that collectively accommodate several thousand spectators.
leads into a concert hall through a triple-height atrium
The heart of the building is the main concert hall, solved in “box in box” room, to ensure optimal acoustics.
